positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Decreased code duplication and increased reusability by writing an adaptable module to reclaim message channel resources such as heap storage -- allows three other major system subcomponents to leverage the same module yielding more maintainable and robust code.

Increased zSystems error tolerance by designing and implementing recovery algorithms that properly recover tasks that are in flight on outstanding work queues in a multi-processor computing environment in the event of a hardware failure, memory access failure, or other task failures yielding highly recoverable firmware.

 Implemented a solution that recognizes and recovers only the memory structures associated with a failure alleviating the expense of indiscriminately scanning through all structures associated with a resource.

 Reduced the time required to recover from a system error by implementing a recovery algorithm in-line with normal mainline operations for the outstanding work associated with a failing resource

Developed and deployed a tool known as ‘Problem Analysis using Machine Learning for z Systems’ (PAM-on-z) to IBM’s cloud platform, Bluemix, to assist debuggers, customer-facing support teams, and test engineers in recognizing system errors by applying classification machine-learning algorithms to hardware system logs.

 Reduced the time to debug known errors by more than 70% for problem analysis experts by deploying PAM-on-z to the IBM cloud platform.

Led a team of 5 engineers in the development and delivery of PAM-on-z leveraging common agile development methodologies

 Developed a way to more accurately measure message channel activity over an InfiniBand Architected network providing real-time resource utilization analysis to customers (patent pending)

Debug and patch complex problems discovered by our test organization adhering to principles set forth in continuous integration and continuous delivery

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Increased the performance of the computational intensive VASP code by removing inner-loop dependencies for increased vectorization (SIMD)

Refactored code to be thread safe to distribute iterations of large for-loops across OpenMP threads increasing parallelization.

Decrease the latency involved with going out to main memory by moving frequently accessed arrays to on chip, high-bandwidth memory.

Increased overall runtime performance of code by 17%

company.name: National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center (NERSC)

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
Investigated the relationship between features in geo-social datasets in order to re-aggregate datasets in one geographical units such as zip codes to counties

Models the weight of various features such as population, household incomes, neighborhood density, etc. from a populations dataset to see the role it plays in crime rates and the number of restaurants through the application of linear regression

company.name: University of Michigan College of Engineering

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Created a central repository to store the attributes of various objects modeled by the simulator to increase maintainability and library portability across other product simulators.

 Increased retrieval performance of an object’s attributes from the repository by moving data from arrays and vectors to hash tables yielding a retrieval time complexity of O(1) vs O(n)

Made recommendation on equipment upgrades based on network test involving server outages, packet
